conflicts.description: The Chartwrights demand all enclaves pool their Weaving to repair the failing skybridges; the Shepherds refuse to give up song they earned, and the Order refuses to teach its rites at all — a three-way stalemate while the threads fray.
conflicts.name: The Song-Sharing Dispute

conflicts.description: Salvagers from Marrowdeep strip thread-glass from weakened spans to sell back at a price, accelerating the decay they claim to merely profit from.
conflicts.name: The Untethered Raids

conflicts.description: Whispers grow that Kelvara and Thalorin might cut their tethers and drift free as a paired realm, abandoning Vesperine and the Under-isle — a plan the Untethered quietly encourage.
conflicts.name: The Drift Secession

description: Aethermoor is a fractured archipelago of floating islands adrift in an endless sky-sea of luminous cloud. Once a single continent, the realm shattered centuries ago in the Sundering, and its scattered landmasses survived only because the ancient Weavers raised the skybridges — ribbons of woven starlight and stone that still bind the isles together. Now the bridges are fraying. Enclaves that once traded freely have grown suspicious and insular, each hoarding the dwindling bridge-song that keeps their island tethered. Wondrous airships of sail and silk ply the winds between isles, cartographers chart the slow drift of the land, and every child learns the old rhyme: when the last skybridge falls, the isles fall with it. A young cartographer who can read the fading bridge-threads may be the realm's only hope of weaving the rival enclaves back into one people before Aethermoor scatters forever into the cloud-dark below.

factions.description: Cartographers and wind-sailors of Vesperine who map the drifting isles. They were first to prove the skybridges are failing, and they argue the enclaves must share bridge-song freely to survive — a position that threatens every power that profits from scarcity.
factions.name: The Chartwrights' Guild

factions.description: Farmers and anchor-wardens who maintain the eastern skybridge tethers. Proud and practical, they believe their labor holds the realm together and resent the Guild's demand that they surrender song they wove themselves.
factions.name: The Shepherds of Kelvara

factions.description: Mystic monks of Thalorin who alone remember the full rites of bridge-mending. They refuse to choose a side, insisting the Weaving is sacred and cannot be sold or shared — even as the bridges they serve come undone.
factions.name: The Order of the Last Weave

factions.description: Salvagers, exiles, and free-booters of Marrowdeep who claim the skybridges are a chain, not a lifeline. Some raid the spans for thread-glass; others quietly prepare to survive the coming Scatter.
factions.name: The Untethered

history.description: The single continent of old Aethermoor shattered into drifting isles in a cataclysm whose cause is still disputed. Thousands were lost to the cloud-dark in the first year.
history.name: The Sundering

history.description: The first Weavers sang the original skybridges into being, binding the surviving isles before they could scatter. The Order of the Last Weave traces its founding to this rite.
history.name: The First Weaving

history.description: Enclaves sworn to maintain their bridge-anchors signed the Drift Law, formalizing trade routes and tether duties across the archipelago.
history.name: The Drift Accords

history.description: Survivors of a minor isle's fall refused to abandon their wreck and built a hanging city beneath the archipelago, outside the Accords' protection.
history.name: The Settling of Marrowdeep

history.description: Guild chartwrights first documented systematic decay in the skybridge threads — a slow unravelling dismissed by the enclaves as alarmism.
history.name: The Great Fraying

history.description: A neglected skybridge between two minor isles gave way; both landmasses drifted into the cloud-dark, proving the Guild's warnings true and igniting the present crisis.
history.name: The Loss of the Silent Span

locations.description: The largest isle and seat of the Chartwrights' Guild, Vesperine is a tiered city of mapmaker towers whose glass lanterns glow amber at dusk. Its great Atlas Spire holds the Drift Charts that track the slow migration of every island in the archipelago.
locations.name: Vesperine

locations.description: A windswept pastoral isle of terraced skyfarms and singing windmills, Kelvara feeds half the realm. Its people tend the bridge-anchors on the eastern span and distrust outsiders who come asking questions about the fraying tethers.
locations.name: Kelvara

locations.description: A mist-shrouded isle of monasteries built around the oldest surviving skybridge anchor. The monks of Thalorin keep the Weaving — the songcraft that repairs bridge-threads — and guard its secrets jealously.
locations.name: Thalorin

locations.description: The Under-isle: a shadowed landmass hanging beneath the main archipelago, lit by cave-crystal and geothermal vents. Salvagers and exiles make their home here, scavenging fragments of fallen islands and whispering that the bridges were never meant to hold.
locations.name: Marrowdeep

name: Aethermoor

rules.statement: Islands drift apart on the sky-currents; only a living skybridge or a moored tether-line can hold two landmasses in fixed relation, and every bridge decays without regular renewal of its thread-song.
Bridge-mending requires the Weaving — a sung rite that draws thread-glass into new strands. Each weaving costs the singer years of memory, which is why the Order rations its use.

Aethermoor's peoples fight with harpoon-lines, sail-gliders, and song-forged blades; there is no combustion technology anywhere in the archipelago, and the under-cloud's volatile mists would make it suicidal anyway.
By ancient Drift Law, any enclave that abandons its bridge-anchor forfeits claim to its neighbors' routes — a rule that now tempts desperate isles to cut loose and drift free.
An island that loses every tether does not sink; it drifts beyond the charted winds and is lost to the cloud-dark, never seen again.
Thread-glass, the raw stuff of skybridges, can only be gathered where a fallen isle once touched the sky — most easily found in the wrecks beneath Marrowdeep.
